research.headline: Jailbreak Detection on Large Language Models via Contrastive Prototype Structures
research.summary: Jailbreak attempts and harmful prompts remain a challenge for the safe deployment of large language models. We study whether contrastively learned representations can support safety detection without training an additional downstream classifier. We propose Jailbreak Detection with Prototype Inference (JDPI), which uses binary safety labels to construct harmful and benign prototypes and makes predictions from relative prototype distances.

research.headline: Building AI that can work across the enterprise
research.summary: For years, enterprises have approached AI as a series of discrete experiments. Now, as AI agents begin to move into the workflows that run the business, that model is starting to look inadequate. Organizations moving from isolated pilots toward AI agents and autonomous workflows are confronting a deeper challenge: rethinking how data, business processes, governance,….

research.headline: Mapping the AI Supply Chain: Dependencies, Vulnerabilities, and Market Concentration in the AI Ecosystem
research.summary: AI systems are built across many organizations that contribute models, data, compute, capital, talent, and other assets. While the layers of the AI stack are relatively well understood, the relationships between actors and components across layers remains sparsely documented. In this work, we focus on the organizations that make up the AI supply chain: the complex network of actors that contribute to the development and deployment of AI.

research.headline: Agentic Harness Engineering Beta: Requirement-Centered Evolution of Agent Harnesses
research.summary: Real-world harness engineering is driven by explicit and implicit user requirements, which guide development and validation. However, existing harness evolution methods often overlook implicit requirements and interaction needs, while using a single evolution agent to modify the harness and benchmark scores to select changes. This process often produces narrow patches and leads to benchmark-specific local optima.

research.headline: Decomposing SGD Dynamics in Neural Networks: Teacher-Induced Spikes and Variance Inflation
research.summary: We study two-layer neural networks trained by stochastic gradient descent (SGD) on a multi-index teacher model, focusing on how first-layer parameters orthogonal to the teacher subspace affect generalization. We decompose the first-layer weights into a signal component aligned with the teacher and an orthogonal complement, and analyze their joint SGD dynamics together with the second layer in the proportional limit. We show that although SGD updates to the complement are initially isotropic, the training dynamics induce teacher-dependent spectral spikes in the complement Gram matrix.

regulatory.headline: FTC Sues to Block Covetrus Acquisition of MWI
regulatory.summary: The Federal Trade Commission sued to block Covetrus Inc. from acquiring its closest competitor, MWI Veterinary Supply Inc., in a $3.5 billion deal. The FTC alleges the combination of the two largest veterinary product distributors will drive up costs for clinics and pet owners.

regulatory.headline: FTC and 17 States Secure $63 Million Settlement with Family Dollar Stores in Price Transparency Win for Consumers
regulatory.summary: Family Dollar has generated millions of dollars by charging more at the register than the prices it advertises, the FTC and states allege Family Dollar will pay $63 million to settle Federal Trade Commission and state allegations that the company routinely charged customers more at the register than the prices displayed on shelves, price tags and advertisements, costing consumers millions of dollars.

regulatory.headline: FTC Takes Enforcement Action Against Safety-Harness Manufacturer for Allegedly False Made in the USA Claims
regulatory.summary: FTC’s proposed order requires the company to stop making deceptive claims and pay a monetary judgment The Federal Trade Commission is taking action against Elk River Inc., an Alabama-based manufacturer of safety harnesses and other fall protection equipment for workers, for falsely claiming that its harnesses are “Made in USA.”.

frontier.headline: CREST: A Hardware-Aware GNN-Based Framework for High-Fidelity and Robust Superconducting Quantum Compilation
frontier.summary: Quantum compilation on superconducting processors requires selecting a connected execution region whose topology and calibrated properties suit the input circuit. This choice constrains subsequent routing and influences the noise encountered during execution, yet aggregate hardware-quality metrics alone may not reliably predict the execution fidelity of a given circuit. Calibration updates can also change region suitability and trigger the rebuilding of calibration-dependent resource structures.

frontier.headline: Something strange is living beneath the skin of deep-sea pigs
frontier.summary: Scientists have discovered a strange bacterium hiding beneath the skin of deep-sea creatures known as sea pigs, revealing an unexpected biological partnership. The microbe has an unusually tiny genome, yet more than a quarter of its DNA is devoted to making surface proteins, some of them exceptionally large. Researchers suspect it depends heavily on its host for survival, but what the sea pigs gain in return remains a mystery.

frontier.headline: Scientists tested 212 plant-based foods. Every single one contained fungal toxins
frontier.summary: A new study has uncovered a surprising concern hiding in popular plant-based foods and drinks. Researchers tested 212 vegan and vegetarian products sold in the UK, including meat alternatives, oat milk, almond milk, and soy milk, and found that every single one contained at least one potentially harmful fungal toxin. Known as mycotoxins, these naturally occurring compounds can contaminate grains, legumes, and seeds during farming and storage.

frontier.headline: Quantum Simulation of First-Quantised Chemistry with a Sum-of-Squares Representation
frontier.summary: Calculating molecular energies is expected to be an important application of quantum computers, but the most efficient algorithms to achieve this typically have significant space requirements. Scaling quantum processors to thousands of logical qubits is a daunting engineering challenge, so developing algorithms that run with reduced qubit requirements is of particular importance. Moreover, most algorithms are benchmarked on active spaces with about as many orbitals as electrons, missing dynamical correlation which is necessary to describe real chemistry.

frontier.headline: A Nonsecular Quantum Master Equation with Detailed Balance and Second-order Error Bound
frontier.summary: An effective theory of open quantum systems should preserve the detailed balance structure inherited from microscopic reversibility and remain accurate throughout relaxation. Meeting both requirements is particularly challenging in quantum many-body systems, where dense spectra can invalidate the secular approximation even at weak coupling. Here we construct a nonsecular quantum master equation that satisfies time-reversal Kubo-Martin-Schwinger (TR-KMS) detailed balance.

voices.headline: ‘No Take, Only Throw’ Politics
voices.summary: This month, fed-up, stressed-out Americans headed to the ballot box and tacked hard to the left, supporting the party that is promising to restore billions of dollars in federal spending and billions of dollars in federal tax revenue. Democrats won in blue states. They won in purple states, such as Georgia, Michigan, Maine, and North Carolina.

voices.headline: Black Politicians Can Be Like This
voices.summary: When Keisha Lance Bottoms, the next governor of Georgia, announced her transition team, one name in particular stood out: Tyler Perry, the filmmaker most famous for playing Madea, a Black matriarch who puffs on cigarettes and disciplines smart-aleck children, and who can draw out a “hello” with so many southern syllables that it sounds like “hallelujah.” Perry’s movies may be frowned upon, especially by members of the Black elite. Some people thought Bottoms’s pick was in poor taste (or, as one New York magazine writer put it, “unserious” ). But others—myself included—were here for it.

voices.headline: Can Pope Leo Bridge the Church’s Demographic Divide?
voices.summary: Pope Leo XIV is leading the Catholic Church during a period of extraordinary demographic change. A century ago, Europeans dominated the Church, representing some two-thirds of the world’s Catholics. Today, Latin America and Africa together make up a majority.

voices.headline: Election Denialism Is All but Dead
voices.summary: O ut of all the surprises of the 2026 midterm election, among the most heartening was Donald Trump’s willingness to accept the results. “We’ll probably work something out,” he told The New York Times of the incoming Democratic majority in Congress. The next day, he walked the press around the site of the planned White House ballroom, less interested in battling over the election than showing off his construction project.
